bivy.name: Lunch Counter
bivy.notes: The standard high camp for the South Climb and effectively the only sheltered ground on the route, a wide rubble bench under Suksdorf Ridge about four miles and 3,700 ft above Cold Springs. It sits anywhere from roughly 9,200 to 9,400 ft because the bench is long and people camp at both ends rather than at one spot. The rock walls left by earlier parties are the whole reason to camp here — wind funnels across the bench and an unprotected tent takes a beating — so plan on repairing a wall rather than finding a perfect one. The summit ridge east of here forms the Yakama Nation boundary; the South Climb stays on Forest Service ground, but do not descend or traverse east off the standard line.
bivy.water: Snowmelt only, and seasonal. Running meltwater usually appears at the upper end of the bench through early and mid summer, but it is not dependable — in a thin snow year or by late season the bench can be dry, so carry a stove and fuel to melt snow.
bivy.permit: Cascade Volcano Pass (Mt. Adams Climbing Pass) required — this camp is above the 7,000 ft threshold that triggers it between May 1 and Sept 30. Bought through recreation.gov, valid for a single climbing trip; carry it and leave a copy in the windshield. Parking at the South Climb trailhead needs a recreation pass, and the climbing pass parking stub satisfies that within Mt. Adams Wilderness in season. Outside that window or below 7,000 ft, a free self-issued wilderness permit is what applies. Human waste must be packed out in the supplied bags.
bivy.capacity: Large — dozens of parties on summer weekends, spread across a broad bench; scores of pre-built rock windbreaks, though the best-sheltered ones fill first

bivy.name: Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead
bivy.notes: Most South Climb parties sleep here the night before, either to acclimatise a little or to get an alpine start without carrying a camp to the Lunch Counter. Facilities are primitive — a vault toilet, no piped water, no developed fee sites. Access is FR 80 to FR 8040 and then FR 8040-500, roughly eight miles of washboarded and rutted gravel with the last three miles steep, narrow and switchbacked; ordinary cars get up it at low speed but a low-slung vehicle can bottom out, and RVs and trailers should not attempt it. The road generally opens around mid-May and is usually clear of snow by the start of July, so early-season parties should expect to park lower and walk.
bivy.water: Unreliable. Treat this as a dry camp and arrive with water. Small springs and Morrison Creek near the road can be running early in the season and gone by late summer.
bivy.permit: A recreation pass is required to park — Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency pass, or a day pass; a valid Mt. Adams Climbing Pass parking stub also works between May 1 and Sept 30. Camping here is below the 7,000 ft climbing-pass threshold, so a free self-issued wilderness permit covers you unless you go above that line. Waste bags are usually stocked at the trailhead.
bivy.capacity: Small — a handful of primitive sites plus overflow in the parking area; fills on summer weekends

bivy.name: Morrison Creek Campground
bivy.notes: The fallback camp when the upper road defeats a vehicle or when Cold Springs is full, about three miles below the South Climb trailhead on the same road. The 2012 Cascade Creek fire burned through here, so shade is patchy and there is standing dead timber to consider when choosing a tent spot in wind. Camping here means driving or walking the last steep section to the trailhead in the morning, which costs about an hour but keeps the option open when the road is rough.
bivy.water: Morrison Creek runs beside the camp but is seasonal and can be low or dry by late summer; treat what you take and do not count on it in August or September.
bivy.permit: No climbing pass needed at this elevation — it sits well below the 7,000 ft line. A free self-issued wilderness permit covers travel into Mt. Adams Wilderness from here, and a recreation pass applies at the trailheads above.
bivy.capacity: Small — a handful of primitive sites, several strung along the creek

access.fees: Mt. Adams Climbing Pass required above 7,000 ft, May 1-Sept 30
access.notes: Mount Adams Climbing Pass required (May 1-Sep 30, age 16+). Fee via Recreation.gov. Mount Adams Wilderness, USFS.
access.rules: Group size capped at 12. Human waste must be packed out above 7,000 ft (blue/WAG bags) — free bags available at the Trout Lake Ranger District office, no collection service. The Mazama Glacier route and Bird Creek Meadows/Round-the-Mountain area cross Yakama Nation land and require a separate small tribal recreation permit purchased at Bird Creek Meadows — the standard South Climb/Cold Springs route stays on Forest Service land and does not.
access.permit: Cascade Volcano Pass / Mt. Adams Climbing Pass via recreation.gov
access.seasonal: South Climb route typically opens as snow melts out around May.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest; Mount Adams Wilderness
access.land_manager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Mt. Adams Ranger District) — Mount Adams Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Cold Springs/South Climb Trailhead day-use fee: $5/vehicle/day or $30/year (a Northwest Forest Pass satisfies this; the Climbing Pass’s parking stub also covers it May 1–Sept 30).
